data.description:
Marquee verifies inbound Resend delivery webhooks correctly and receives none of them, because no
webhook endpoint has ever been registered on the Resend account. The signing secret currently on the
Worker is a random placeholder set to unblock a deploy.

## What is already true (do not rebuild this)

- `src/routes/resend-webhook.routes.ts` serves `POST /api/v1/webhooks/resend`, public + rate-limited.
- `src/lib/inbound-delivery.ts` `verifySvixSignature()` implements Svix correctly: HMAC over
  `${svix-id}.${svix-timestamp}.${raw body}`, freshness tolerance, raw body signed before parse,
  missing `svix-id` rejected as unauthenticated.
- `parseResendDeliveryEvent()` handles exactly four event types: `email.delivered`, `email.bounced`,
  `email.complained`, `email.delivery_delayed`. Everything else returns null and is acked with no effect.
- `applyResendDeliveryEvent()` joins by `provider_message_id`, applies in provider event order, and is
  replay-safe on event id.
- Migration `0014_inbound_delivery_state.sql` IS applied to production D1 (verified 2026-08-12).
- `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is declared at `wrangler.jsonc:162` in `secrets.required`.

The code is complete. This ticket is configuration, not implementation.

## Evidence of the gap

    GET https://api.resend.com/webhooks  ->  200
    {"object":"list","has_more":false,"data":[]}

Zero endpoints. No events are being sent to anyone.

## Actions to take

Credentials: `RESEND_API_KEY` (full access) is in
`/Users/atin/Projects/Stage11/code/platform/.credentials/.env`. Service guide:
`/Users/atin/Projects/Stage11/code/platform/resend.md`. Never print a key into a transcript,
a commit, a PR, or this board -- Marquee's repo is destined to be public.

1. Register the endpoint via `POST https://api.resend.com/webhooks`:
   - endpoint URL: `https://marquee.stage11.dev/api/v1/webhooks/resend`
   - events: `email.delivered`, `email.bounced`, `email.complained`, `email.delivery_delayed`
   Subscribe to those four only; the parser ignores the rest, so extra subscriptions are pure noise.
   Confirm the exact request field names against Resend's current API rather than assuming
   `endpoint_url`/`events` -- a wrong body fails loudly, which is fine, but do not guess twice.
   THE SIGNING SECRET IS RETURNED ONCE, AT CREATION. Capture it in that same step or you will be
   deleting the endpoint and making a new one to get it.

2. Set it on the Worker, replacing the placeholder:
       npx wrangler secret put RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET
   Takes effect immediately. No deploy, no downtime. Run it from a deploy shell with
   `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN="$MARQUEE_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN"` exported, per DEPLOY.md.

3. Verify end to end, not by status code. Send one real email through the app and confirm the
   matching `outbox` row moves `delivery_state` from `'unknown'` to `'delivered'`. A 200 from the
   endpoint proves reachability only -- it returns 200 for unmatched and unsupported events by design.
   State plainly if you could not get a real send through; do not infer success from a signature check.

## Decision the operator should see before step 1

Resend webhooks are ACCOUNT-level, not domain-level. This endpoint will receive delivery events for
every email the Stage 11 Resend account sends, including other projects'. Marquee handles that safely
already (unknown `provider_message_id` is acknowledged without disclosure), so nothing breaks -- but it
means Marquee's endpoint observes other projects' message ids. Worth deciding rather than discovering.
If that is unacceptable, the alternative is a scoped endpoint per project, which Resend may or may not
support at the domain level -- check before promising it.

## Done means

Endpoint registered, real signing secret on the Worker, and one real send observed flipping an outbox
row to `delivered`. Then file what you learned in `code/platform/resend.md` -- it has no webhook
section, and the next project will hit this same wall.
data.title: Inbound Resend delivery webhook is unregistered and unsigned

data.body:
## Held at the operator decision. Nothing was registered.

Atin's call, 2026-08-12: **do not register the endpoint.** The account-level exposure was
put to him before step 1 and he declined it, so this ticket stops after the investigation.
No webhook exists on the Resend account, no secret was changed on the Worker, and the
worktree has no code changes — this was always a configuration ticket, and the configuration
was not made.

### What the investigation confirmed (all read-only)

- `GET https://api.resend.com/webhooks` → `{"object":"list","has_more":false,"data":[]}`.
  Still zero endpoints, unchanged from the ticket's evidence.
- `POST https://marquee.stage11.dev/api/v1/webhooks/resend` with no Svix headers → `401`.
  The route is live and rejecting correctly; that is reachability, not function.
- Live build is `a218bff3573e`. `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is present in `wrangler secret list`
  (the placeholder). `verifySvixSignature()` returns false for any secret not starting with
  `whsec_`, so today a genuine Resend event would be rejected before the HMAC is even computed.
- Production `outbox`: 14 rows, **every one `suppressed`**, zero with a `provider_message_id`.
  No email has ever actually left prod. So there is currently no row that a delivery event
  could match even if one arrived — the ledger is not merely stale, it is empty.

### The scope finding that drove the decision

Resend's create-webhook API takes exactly two fields, `endpoint` and `events`. There is no
`domain_id`, no filter, no scoping of any kind — the response carries `id`, `object`, and
`signing_secret`. Account-level is not a default that can be narrowed; it is the only shape
the API offers. So the real choice was "every Stage 11 project's delivery events land on
Marquee's Worker" or "no delivery events at all," and the operator chose the latter.

### Consequence, stated plainly

The inbound delivery feature stays inert. `outbox.delivery_state` will remain `'unknown'`
for every row indefinitely, and the delivery-health screen has no real provider truth behind
it. This is now a deliberate product state rather than an unnoticed gap, which is the actual
value this ticket delivered. Anyone reading the delivery-health surface should understand it
is reporting on data no provider is feeding.

### Exact runbook, if this is ever reversed

Step 1 — register (this is the step that needs the operator's word, not the agent's):

```sh
set -a; source ~/Projects/Stage11/code/platform/.credentials/.env; set +a
curl -s -X POST https://api.resend.com/webhooks \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESEND_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "endpoint": "https://marquee.stage11.dev/api/v1/webhooks/resend",
    "events": ["email.delivered","email.bounced","email.complained","email.delivery_delayed"]
  }'
```

`signing_secret` (`whsec_…`) comes back **once**. Capture it in that same step into a shell
variable — never echo it, never let it reach a file — or the endpoint has to be deleted and
recreated to get another.

Step 2 — replace the placeholder on the Worker. Takes effect immediately, no deploy:

```sh
export CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN="$MARQUEE_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN"
npx wrangler secret put RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET   # paste at the prompt; do not pass on argv
```

Step 3 — the live-send path, which I traced and which needs no data surgery. The prod event
`evt_aie-ny-2026` is `demo_mode=1`, so ordinary mail is suppressed unless the address is in
the `demo_safe_allowlist` event setting — and there is no route that writes that setting.
But two senders carry `send_policy='always_live'` and bypass suppression entirely, and one of
them is reachable from outside: `enqueuePublicFormConfirmation`, the public CFP confirmation.
Demo mode also exempts the public form from Turnstile (`publicTurnstileExempt` returns true
when `demo_mode=1`). So submitting `/f/cfp` with a real address is a genuine user-path live
send, over the API, with nothing stubbed:

```sh
# submit the public CFP with a real deliverable address (operator picked projects@stage11.ai)
# then watch the row that must flip:
npx wrangler d1 execute DB --remote --command \
  "SELECT id, to_email, status, provider_message_id, delivery_state, delivered_at
   FROM outbox WHERE provider_message_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 5;"
```

Done means that row moves `delivery_state` from `'unknown'` to `'delivered'`. A 200 from the
webhook endpoint proves nothing — the route returns 200 for unmatched and unsupported events
by design. Only the row changing is evidence.

The other `always_live` sender, `enqueueSmokeHarnessMail`, is **not** usable for this:
`npm run smoke:mail` is still a stub pointing at MRQ-24.

### Filed elsewhere

`code/platform/resend.md` had no webhook section. Added one covering the account-level
constraint, the create call and its once-only secret, and the Svix verification contract, so
the next Stage 11 project meets this decision already framed instead of rediscovering it.
That file is in the Stage11 monorepo, so it is a separate commit from this repo.

provenance.reason: Operator declined account-level webhook registration (Atin, 2026-08-12). Investigation complete; runbook filed in comments if reversed.
